ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown, the $\triangle ODC$ is obtained by rotating $\triangle OAB$ clockwise by $30^\circ$ around point $O$. If point $D$ falls exactly on $AB$, and the measure of $\angle AOC$ is $100^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\triangle ODC$ is rotated clockwise by $30^\circ$ around point O to get $\triangle OAB$,\\
it follows that AO=DO, and $\angle AOD=\angle BOC=30^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle A=\angle ADO=(180^\circ-30^\circ)\div 2=75^\circ$,\\
Given that $\angle AOC=100^\circ$,\\
it then follows that $\angle DOB=\angle AOC-\angle AOD-\angle BOC=100^\circ-30^\circ-30^\circ=40^\circ$,\\
Since $\angle ADO=\angle B+\angle DOB$,\\
it follows that $\angle B=\angle ADO-\angle DOB=75^\circ-40^\circ=\boxed{35^\circ}$.

Given that $\angle AOC=100^\circ$, it then follows that $\angle DOB=\angle AOC-\angle AOD-\angle BOC=100^\circ-30^\circ-30^\circ=40^\circ$. Since $\angle ADO=\angle B+\angle DOB$, it follows that $\angle B=\angle ADO-\angle DOB=75^\circ-40^\circ=\boxed{35^\circ}$.

The rays drawn from O in clockwise order are OA, OD, OB, OC, and line segments such as DC and OB are also connected in the figure.

Reasoning: The problem statement gives that △ODC is obtained by rotating △OAB clockwise by 30° about point O, so O is fixed, A corresponds to D, and B corresponds to C. Therefore AO=DO, and ∠AOD=30°, ∠BOC=30°. In triangle AOD, because AO=DO, it is an isosceles triangle, with vertex angle ∠AOD=30°, so the base angles ∠OAD=∠ADO=(180°−30°)/2=75°. Also because D is on AB, ∠OAD is the ∠A of △OAB, that is, ∠A=75°. It is known that ∠AOC=100°, and the order of the rays is OA, OD, OB, OC, so ∠DOB=∠AOC−∠AOD−∠BOC=100°−30°−30°=40°. Therefore ∠AOB=∠AOD+∠DOB=30°+40°=70°. In △OAB, ∠B=180°−∠A−∠AOB=180°−75°−70°=35°.
